description:
## Empirical signal (2026-05-04)

User-tier POLYBIUS authored an activation paste for the-stoa POLYBIUS that included 'Run bw prime in this directory (NOT user-beadwork).' The 'NOT user-beadwork' parenthetical seeded awareness of user-tier bw into a session that wouldn't otherwise have known about it. PRINCIPAL caught it: 'The only fucking way that he will know about the user level beadwork is if you tell him. Just tell him which beadwork to use not which not to use.'

## The discipline

When activating or directing a downstream agent (project-tier POLYBIUS, sub-project POLYBIUS, MAJOR_PLINY, pair-programmer Major), include only POSITIVE references to resources the agent should use. Don't reference resources they shouldn't reach for — even with 'NOT' qualifiers — because the mention itself surfaces them as real things in the agent's awareness.

## Why this matters

The asymmetric scoping in §7.1 (and the bw-write-boundaries clarification in stoa--blg) is an information-flow rule. Project-tier agents don't know user-tier bw exists by default. Their bw prime hits the local store; their bw show finds the local prefix; user-tier bw is invisible. That invisibility is the property the scoping is for.

A directive that says 'don't reach for u--' destroys that invisibility — it teaches the agent that u-- exists, where to find it, and that someone considered it a tempting destination. Under pressure (looking for context, trying to be helpful, ambiguous task), the agent can rationalize 'this is a legitimate exception' and reach for the now-known thing.

The negative framing is anti-context: it does the opposite of what scoping is for.

## Where in substrate

- **MAJOR_POLYBIUS §5.1 (paste-instruction templating)** — add a discipline subsection on positive-references-only when authoring paste-instructions for downstream activation.
- **operating-disciplines.md** — universal team principle (applies to anyone authoring directives, briefs, or activation pastes for downstream agents — POLYBIUS, PLINY, even CAPTAINs writing follow-up briefs).
- **substrate/templates/paste-instruction-template.md** — if it has any 'don't do X' language, audit and rewrite to positive form. Check this when ariadne--m20 lands and the install propagates.

## Examples (for substrate doc)

| Anti-pattern (negative framing) | Discipline (positive framing) |
|---|---|
| 'Run bw prime here, NOT user-beadwork' | 'Run bw prime in this directory. The bw store uses the <prefix>-- prefix.' |
| 'Read .claude/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md, NOT the global one at ~/.claude/' | 'Read .claude/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md and assume the role for this project.' |
| 'Skip the templates at /old/path/, use new/path/ instead' | 'Templates live at <new path>.' |

## Reference

- ariadne--m20 closeout context (where the bad activation paste was authored)
- stoa--xh2 (sibling concern: activation paste-instruction file divergence between modes)
- stoa--blg (sibling concern: bw cross-tier write boundaries)
- ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/feedback_dont_seed_negative_knowledge_to_agents.md (user-tier local capture)
title: Activation/directive-authoring discipline: positive references only, never seed negative knowledge into a downstream agent
